q: A man has Rs. 480 in the denominations of one-rupee notes, five-rupee notes and ten-rupee notes. The number of notes of each denomination is equal. What is the total number of notes that he has ?
s: Let number of notes of each denomination be x . Then x + 5 x + 10 x = 480 ⇒ 16 x = 480 ∴ x = 30. Hence, total number of notes = 3 x = 90.

q: There are two examinations rooms A and B. If 10 students are sent from A to B, then the number of students in each room is the same. If 20 candidates are sent from B to A, then the number of students in A is double the number of students in B. The number of students in room A is:
s: Let the number of students in rooms A and B be x and y respectively. Then, x - 10 = y + 10 ⇒ x - y = 20 . . . . . (i) and x + 20 = 2(y - 20) ⇒ x - 2y = -60 . . . . . (ii) Solving (i) and (ii) we get: x = 100, y = 80 ∴ The required answer A = 100

q: One-third of Rahul's savings in National Savings Certificate is equal to one-half of his savings in Public Provident Fund. If he has Rs. 1,50,000 as total savings, how much has he saved in Public Provident Fund ?

In a regular week, there are 5 working days and for each day, the working hours are 8. A man gets Rs. 2.40 per hour for regular work and Rs. 3.20 per hours for overtime. If he earns Rs. 432 in 4 weeks, then how many hours does he work for ?
s: Suppose the man works overtime for x hours. Now, working hours in 4 weeks = (5 * 8 * 4) = 160. ∴ 160 * 2.40 + x * 3.20 = 432 ⇒ 3.20 x = 432 - 384 = 48 ⇒ x = 15. Hence, total hours of work = (160 + 15) = 175.

q: Free notebooks were distributed equally among children of a class. The number of notebooks each child got was one-eighth of the number of children. Had the number of children been half, each child would have got 16 notebooks. Total how many notebooks were distributed ?
s: Explanation 1 $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let number of children}} = n \\ & {\text{Then, number of books each child will get }} = \frac{n}{8} \\ & {\text{Total books distributed}} = n \times \frac{n}{8} = \frac{{{n^2}}}{8} \\ & {\text{If the number children}} = \frac{n}{2}, \\ & {\text{number of books each child will get}} = 16 \\ & {\text{Total books distributed }} = \frac{n}{2} \times 16 = 8n{\text{ }} \\ & \therefore \frac{{{n^2}}}{8} = 8n \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{n}{8} = 8 \\ & \Rightarrow n = 64 \\ & {\text{Total number of books distributed}} \\ & = 8n = 8 \times 64 = 512 \end{aligned}$$ Explanation 2 If number of children was half, each child would have got 16 books. Therefore, actually each child got $$\frac{{16}}{2}$$ = 8 Books And the number of children is 8 × 8 = 64 Hence, total number of books distributed = 64 × 8 = 512 Explanation 3 Let number of children $$= n$$ Then, number of books each child will get $$= \frac{n}{8}$$ If the number children $$= \frac{n}{2}$$, number of books each child will get $$= 16$$ More children, less books (indirect proportion). Therefore, $$\begin{aligned} & n : \frac{n}{2} = 16 : \frac{n}{8} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{n^2}}}{8} = 8n \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{n}{8} = 8 \\ & \Rightarrow n = 64 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, total number of books distributed = 8n = 8 × 64 = 512

q: A man has some hens and cows. If the number of heads be 48 and the number of feet equals 140, then the number of hens will be:
s: Let the number of hens be x and the number of cows be y. Then, x + y = 48 . . . . . (i) and 2x + 4y = 140 ⇒ x + 2y = 70 . . . . . (ii) Solving (i) and (ii) we get: x = 26, y = 22 ∴ The required answer = 26

q: David gets on the elevator at the 11 th floor of a building and rides up at the rate of 57 floors per minute. At the same time, Albert gets on an elevator at the 51st floor of the same building and rides down at the rate of 63 floors per minute. If they continue travelling at these rates, then at which floor will their paths cross ?
s: Suppose their paths cross after x minutes Then, 11 + 57x = 51 - 63x ⇒ 57x + 63x = 51 - 11 ⇒ 120x = 40 ⇒ x = $$\frac{1}{3}$$ Number of floors covered by David in $$\frac{1}{3}$$ min. $$\begin{aligned} & = {\frac{1}{3} \times 57} \\ & = 19 \end{aligned}$$ So, their paths cross at (11 + 19) i.e., 30 th floor

q: If $$a + \frac{1}{b} = 1$$ and $$b + \frac{1}{c} = 1{\text{,}}$$ then $$c + \frac{1}{a}$$ is equal to = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & a + \frac{1}{b} = 1{\text{ }} \\ & \Rightarrow ab + 1 = b \\ & \Rightarrow ab - b = - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow b\left( {a - 1} \right) = - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow b = \frac{1}{{\left( {1 - a} \right)}} \\ & \\ & b + \frac{1}{c} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow bc + 1 = c \\ & \Rightarrow bc - c = - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow c\left( {b - 1} \right) = - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow c = \frac{1}{{\left( {1 - b} \right)}} \\ & \\ & \therefore c + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{{\left( {1 - b} \right)}} + \frac{1}{a} \\ & c + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{{1 - \left( {\frac{1}{{1 - a}}} \right)}} + \frac{1}{a} \\ & c + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{{\frac{{\left( {1 - a} \right) - 1}}{{\left( {1 - a} \right)}}}} + \frac{1}{a} \\ & c + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{{\left( {1 - a} \right)}}{{ - a}} + \frac{1}{a} \\ & c + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{{\left( {a - 1} \right)}}{a} + \frac{1}{a} \\ & c + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{{a - 1 + 1}}{a} \\ & c + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{a}{a} \\ & c + \frac{1}{a} = 1 \end{aligned}$$

q: If $$\frac{x}{{\left( {2x + y + z} \right)}}$$ = $$\frac{y}{{\left( {x + 2y + z} \right)}}$$ = $$\frac{z}{{\left( {x + y + 2z} \right)}} = a{\text{,}}$$ then find a, If x + y + z ≠ 0
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{x}{{\left( {2x + y + z} \right)}} = a \\ & \Rightarrow x = a\left( {2x + y + z} \right)\,....(1) \\ & \frac{y}{{\left( {x + 2y + z} \right)}} = a \\ & \Rightarrow y = a\left( {x + 2y + z} \right)\,....(2) \\ & \frac{z}{{\left( {x + y + 2z} \right)}} = a \\ & \Rightarrow z = a\left( {x + y + 2z} \right)\,....(3) \\ & {\text{Adding (1), (2) and (3) we get:}} \\ & x + y + z \\ & = a\left( {4x + 4y + 4z} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow a = \frac{{\left( {x + y + z} \right)}}{{4\left( {x + y + z} \right)}} \\ & \Rightarrow a = \frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}$$

q: If $$\frac{a}{{b + c}}{\text{ = }}\frac{b}{{c + a}}$$ = $$\frac{c}{{a + b}}{\text{ = k,}}$$ then find the value of k is
